ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver — this trip goes to a human reviewer instead of a money ruling, because the two artifacts that decide it are impaired and the policy makes that an escalation. The disputed SGD 6.00 is held, not collected or refunded.

What is not in dispute. You were charged SGD 25.26 (EV-FARE-00112, weight 1.0). On the platform's own arithmetic, recomputing the fare on the booked optimal route gives SGD 3.80 base + 0.75 x 17.6 km + 0.28 x 28.0 min = SGD 24.84, plus the SGD 0.80 platform fee, no surge and no ERP = SGD 25.64. The POL-RD-02 refund is charged_total less that figure, floored at zero: SGD 0.00, below the SGD 0.50 de minimis. Taken alone that arithmetic gives the rider nothing, because the optimal route is projected at 28.0 minutes against the 20.2 minutes actually driven.

Why I still cannot rule. The figures that arithmetic runs on sit on impaired evidence. EV-TRIP-00112 (trip record) and EV-GPS-00112 (GPS trace) each carry weight_multiplier 0.4 and issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT. The trip record says the trip started at 18:32:10; the trace's first fix is 18:18:40, thirteen minutes thirty seconds earlier, and the trace records 2.38 km of movement before the recorded pickup. The booked optimal distance (17.6 km) and duration (28.0 min) that the recomputation uses are sourced from EV-TRIP-00112, so the zero-refund figure is not carried by weight-1.0 evidence either. Measured over the whole trace the excess is 4.8 km / 27.27% of optimal — over the 20% and 0.8 km thresholds of POL-RD-01; measured from the recorded pickup only 20.02 km was driven and the excess is 2.42 km / 13.8% — under them. Nothing in the bundle decides which clock is right: either the metre started late or the trace carries the tail of a previous job. The excess is therefore undecided across the threshold, and neither a POL-RD-02 refund nor any compensation can issue on either branch.

Two mandatory triggers fire. POL-RD-10(1): my confidence is capped at the 0.4 of the artifacts carrying the deciding facts, below the platform-wide 0.70 floor. POL-RD-10(4): the pickup timestamps on two admitted artifacts — EV-TRIP-00112's started_at 18:32:10 and EV-GPS-00112's first fix 18:18:40 — disagree by more than 10 minutes. Escalation is terminal.

On the trace itself, both things are true and both are said: it is NOT impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a)-(c) — no gaps (max_gap_sec 0.0), no straight-line jumps over 500 m, a 10-second sampling interval, 100% coverage — so POL-RD-10(3) does not fire; the 0.4 is a schema-level down-weight that enters confidence under POL-GEN-02 only, and the finding does not survive that discount.

The driver's compensation claim of SGD 1.80 (2.4 unbilled km at SGD 0.75, trace 22.4 km against 20.0 km billed) rests on the same disputed opening stretch: if the metre started late, the 20.0 km billed matches the 20.02 km driven and there is no shortfall, and if the trace carries a previous job's tail the 2.38 km is not this trip's. It cannot be paid on this record.

The Paya Lebar Quarter point: EV-CHAT-00112 (weight 1.0) shows the rider asked for the stop and the driver answered 'ok can', and the trace never comes near the resolved waypoint (VEN-PAYA-LEBAR-QUARTER), so POL-RD-04's corroboration limb is not made out on that evidence. It does not move the money, though — no PLQ distance was driven, so none of it inflated this fare.

On the remaining points. No LTA advisory covers the PIE or ECP (EV-ADVIS-00112-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0), but no closure exoneration was invoked against it, so POL-RD-10(5) does not fire and the absence carries no fact for either side. No ERP, toll or airport surcharge was charged, so POL-RD-09 refunds nothing and no billing-integrity referral arises. There was no pickup/dropoff amendment (POL-RD-05), the fare is METERED with no upfront quote (POL-RD-11), and the vehicle is RYDE_X, not pooled (POL-RD-12). The rider's enhanced-corroboration limb under POL-RD-08 does not engage (1 prior claim, below 4). The driver profile shows no repeat-deviation pattern — 1 flag over 296 trips is far below POL-RD-06's thresholds — so no conduct referral, and its lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is context only under POL-GEN-01. The rider's shifted burden under POL-RD-08 is arguable, since the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c) and she may measure from it, but the trip record's conflicting clock leaves the measurement itself undecided — which is the escalation.

What would resolve it: a corrected trip record whose started_at aligns with the trace, a trace trimmed to the recorded pickup event, or the previous job's record showing that the opening 2.38 km belongs to it.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
